csv_project_name: Design Service for Emergency Operations Center
csv_scope_of_work: The City University of New York (CUNY) is seeking proposals from qualified firms to provide professional assessment, planning, and design services for the development of a Centralized Emergency Operations Center (EOC) at John Jay College of Criminal Justice. Services include evaluating existing conditions and infrastructure, defining operational and technology requirements, developing architectural and engineering designs, preparing technical specifications and supporting documentation, and producing a comprehensive design package for a resilient, scalable, and technology-enabled EOC. The selected consultant will also provide planning-level cost estimates, equipment recommendations, and related advisory services as required.
csv_disciplines_requested: Architecture Services, Interior Design/Space Planning, Programming, Rehabilitation & Refurbishment, Civil Engineering, Surveying/GIS/Mapping

title: Design Services for Emergency Operations Center
short_description: Design of a centralized emergency operations center at John Jay College in New York.
project_location: John Jay College of Criminal Justice, New York, NY, USA
project_scope: Development of a centralized Emergency Operations Center (EOC) at John Jay College of Criminal Justice. Scope includes assessment of existing conditions and infrastructure, definition of operational and technology requirements, architectural and engineering design, technical specifications, supporting documentation, planning-level cost estimates, equipment recommendations, and a comprehensive resilient, scalable, technology-enabled design package. No gross floor area, structural spans, or other quantitative building characteristics are stated.
services: Professional assessment, planning, and design services; architectural and engineering design; technical specifications; supporting documentation; planning-level cost estimating; equipment recommendations; advisory services. Disciplines requested include architecture, interior design/space planning, programming, rehabilitation/refurbishment, civil engineering, and surveying/GIS/mapping.
relevance_explanation:
- Building project with planning and design scope, which gives some early-stage entry potential.
- However, the project is an emergency operations center fit-out/refurbishment type assignment rather than a structurally ambitious new building.
- No indication of long spans, special structures, innovative structural systems, or demanding bridge/roof engineering.
- Focus appears to be architecture, infrastructure assessment, technology requirements, and interior/operational planning.
- Rehabilitation/refurbishment is generally less relevant for sbp than new complex structures.
construction_cost_explanation: No construction cost is stated in the tender notice. The scope mentions that the selected consultant will prepare planning-level cost estimates, indicating costs are not yet defined. Useful known inputs: centralized EOC at an existing college building, likely involving refurbishment, technology integration, resilience upgrades, and architectural/engineering design, but no area or technical quantities are provided, so a realistic estimate is not possible from this notice alone.
fee_explanation: No design fee or budget is stated in the tender notice. The assignment covers assessment, planning, architecture/engineering design, specifications, and advisory services over a 12-month non-renewable contract period, but there is insufficient information to derive a reliable sbp fee estimate.
references_qualifications: Qualified firms are requested to provide professional assessment, planning, and design services for the EOC. No specific minimum number or type of reference projects, fee zones, or detailed qualification thresholds are stated in the notice excerpt.
